notes: Rule 76 gives *his* to τάς: αὐτόν is already spent as the object of ἐπί and so is not available to take the possessive.

The italicized appositional *even* is added under rule 105: the appositive is carried by a bare noun rather than by an expressed preposition, so nothing licenses the word; folding it onto Ἰησοῦς remains defensible and is noted.

ὁ ὀφθείς is read as an appositional substantival article taking the single relativizer *who* under rule 90, the name being anarthrous in the projection and no second-attributive pattern standing for rule 31.
πνεύματος ἁγίου: both anarthrous, so the supplied determiner and the case preposition go with the noun (rules 58 and 21).
